biography: Marcelo Ferraz, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and trepidation in the Opala Old Stock Race paddock, hails from the sun-baked streets of São Paulo. His journey into motorsport wasn't paved with silver spoons but forged in the crucible of street racing. Legend has it that a young Marcelo, barely old enough to reach the pedals, would sneak out his uncle's beat-up Opala, transforming the city's nocturnal avenues into his personal proving ground. One such escapade, witnessed by a retired racing mechanic, led to an apprenticeship and a formal introduction to the world of competitive racing. His raw talent was undeniable, but his aggressive style often led to spectacular crashes and fiery finishes. Currently, at 27, he's a rising star, yet to fully harness his potential, balancing on the razor's edge between brilliance and recklessness. He's actively competing in the Opala Old Stock Race, and aims for greater things.
drivingStyle: Ferraz's driving style is a volatile cocktail of raw aggression and audacious overtaking maneuvers. He's known for late braking and daring dives into corners, often pushing the limits of his Opala and the patience of his rivals. Tire management isn't his forte; he prefers to attack from the outset, sacrificing long-term pace for immediate gains. Under pressure, he becomes even more unpredictable, sometimes cracking under the strain, other times pulling off miraculous saves and victories. He is often seen riding the rumble strips and counter-steering with an almost unnatural ability.

rivalries.reason: A clash of styles – Albuquerque's calculated precision clashes violently with Ferraz's impulsive aggression. Their on-track battles are legendary.
A bitter rivalry stemming from a controversial collision that cost Fonseca a championship title, fueling her determination to always outpace Ferraz.
Rodrigues, known for his rock-solid defensive driving, often frustrates Ferraz's overtaking attempts, leading to heated exchanges both on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears the same faded Senna t-shirt under his race suit.
Refuses to start a race without meticulously polishing his helmet visor.
Has a pre-race ritual of listening to loud samba music while shadow boxing in the garage.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I race to win, even if it means going down in flames."
careerHighlight: Winning the Interlagos Classic race in 2022 after starting from the back of the grid, overtaking 20 cars in a single, rain-soaked lap.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the championship-deciding race in 2023 while leading, handing the title to his arch-rival, Ricardo Albuquerque.
